# Change the teleport power-up (P7) activation key

## Problem Statement
The teleport power-up (P7) is currently activated with the Space key. It needs to be changed to the S key or the down arrow key per product requirement.

## Users
- Player controlling the ship in the GymPowerUpsCombat scene — needs to activate teleport with S or down arrow instead of Space.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 — New activation key:** The teleport power-up activates when the S key or down arrow is pressed (depending on clarification).
- **AC2 — Space key freed:** The Space key is no longer used for teleport activation (and continues to work for other purposes if applicable).
- **AC3 — GDD updated:** The Game Design Document (§3 Controls table, §4.4 P7 Teleport, §6.4) is updated to reflect the new key binding.
- **AC4 — Tests pass:** All existing tests pass; any tests that check for Space key triggering are updated.
- **AC5 — Full test suite passes.**

## Constraints
- Scope is the GymPowerUpsCombat.ts gym scene (main game scene scope TBD).
- Must maintain backward compatibility with test harness (triggerTeleport method).
- Must preserve the FIFO stack behavior and Phase Shift on arrival.

## Existing State
- Teleport activates on Space key (`spaceKey` in `GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` line 272).
- GDD documents Space as the activation key across multiple sections.

## Desired Change
- Change teleport activation from Space to S or down arrow key.
- Update GDD to reflect new key binding.

## Key Files (predicted)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — Change `spaceKey` to use S or down arrow
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update §3, §4.4, §6.4
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` — Update any Space-key dependent tests

## Related Work
- AH-0MTE8EBZ1002U3PX — Unit tests: P7 Teleport (completed)
- AH-0MTE8EBAH007GUO0 — Effects module: teleport (completed)
- AH-0MTE8EBG3004QC66 — Combat gym scene with teleport (completed)

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Risk:** The S key is also used for movement (WASD). This could conflict with downward movement. *Mitigation: Clarify whether both S and down arrow should work, or just one.*
- **Assumption:** Only the gym scene needs updating; the main game scene does not yet have teleport activated.
- **Assumption:** Space key is not needed for shooting or other actions in the gym scene.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should teleport activate on EITHER the S key OR the down arrow key (both work)?" — Answer: **OPEN**
- Q: "Should it be the S key with down arrow as an alternative?" — Answer: **OPEN**
- Q: "Should the Space key still work for other actions (e.g., shooting)?" — Answer: **OPEN**
- Q: "Is the scope limited to the gym scene (GymPowerUpsCombat.ts), or should the main game scene also be updated?" — Answer: **OPEN**

# All power-ups should grow and shrink — Intake Brief (AH-0MTV7MMA6009TIY3)

## Problem statement

All power-up drops should animate from scale 0 → full size on spawn and scale back to 0 before despawning. The combat gym scene already demonstrates this pattern.

## Users

- **Players** — expect visually smooth, satisfying power-up appearance/disappearance animations that make drops easy to track.
- **Gym testers / developers** — want consistent visual behaviour across all gym scenes.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want power-up drops to grow in smoothly so they are easy to spot.
- As a **player**, I want power-up drops to shrink before disappearing so the animation feels deliberate.
- As a **developer**, I want all gym scenes to share the same grow/shrink animation pattern for consistency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — GymPowerUps grows/shrinks:** P5/P8/P9 drops in `GymPowerUps` start at scale 0 and animate to full size (grow window: 0.5 s) then shrink to 0 (shrink window: 0.5 s) before despawning. `advanceDrops()` calls `drop.graphics.setScale(drop.powerUp.currentScale)` each frame.
- [ ] **AC2 — GymPowerUpsCombat grows/shrinks:** P3/P4/P6/P7 drops in `GymPowerUpsCombat` use the same grow/hold/shrink lifecycle, scaling from 0 → 1 → 0.
- [ ] **AC3 — GymWeapons grows/shrinks:** Weapon power-up drops (Spread/Dual/Rapid/Reset) in `GymWeapons` follow the same grow/hold/shrink lifecycle.
- [ ] **AC4 — Collection still works:** Collection gating (3% scale threshold + ship overlap) remains correct throughout the lifecycle.
- [ ] **AC5 — Despawn cleans up:** Fully despawned drops have their Graphics destroyed and removed from the scene.
- [ ] **AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Use the existing `PowerUp` lifecycle class (`PowerUpState`, `currentScale`, `advance(dt)`).
- All gym scenes must be consistent.
- No new assets — visuals are code-drawn (Phaser Graphics).

## Existing state

The `PowerUp` class (`src/powerups/PowerUp.ts`) already implements the full lifecycle with `currentScale` (0 → 1 → 0) and states GROWING/HOLDING/SHRINKING/DESPAWNED.

All three gym scenes already implement grow/shrink:

- `GymPowerUps.ts` — `_spawnDrop` sets `graphics.setScale(0)`; `advanceDrops` sets `graphics.setScale(drop.powerUp.currentScale)`; destroys on DESPAWNED.
- `GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — same pattern: `_spawnDrop` sets scale 0; `advanceDrops` tracks `currentScale`; destroys on despawn.
- `GymWeapons.ts` — same pattern: `_spawnDrop` sets scale 0; `advanceDrops` tracks `currentScale`; destroys on despawn.

This work item was likely created when only the combat gym had the animation; the other scenes were subsequently updated in follow-up work.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` — lifecycle class (already complete)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` — grow/shrink via `currentScale` (already complete)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — grow/shrink via `currentScale` (already complete)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — grow/shrink via `currentScale` (already complete)

## Related work

- `AH-0MTCNZPHN003C5E1` — Power-up core lifecycle + tunable constants (completed)
- `AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40` — Create combat gym scene (completed)
- `AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR` — Weapon power-ups with GymWeapons (completed)
- `AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4` — Power ups need to be larger (completed)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — all gym scenes covered:** The brief says "all power ups" — verified against all three gym scenes. No non-gym power-up rendering exists.
- **Assumption — work is already complete:** Code inspection and tests show the grow/shrink lifecycle is implemented in all scenes. This intake documents the existing state rather than defining new work.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Do not add new animation features (e.g., pulse, glow intensity changes) in this item. Keep to grow/shrink only.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which power-up scenes need grow/shrink?" — Answer: **All gym scenes** — GymPowerUps (P5/P8/P9), GymPowerUpsCombat (P3/P4/P6/P7), GymWeapons (Spread/Dual/Rapid/Reset). Source: code inspection of all three scenes; each already implements the pattern.
- Q: "What is the reference example?" — Answer: **GymPowerUpsCombat** — the work item description says "See the combat powerups scene for an example." All three scenes follow the same pattern (scale 0 at spawn, `currentScale` per frame, destroy on despawn).

## Status assessment

**WORK ALREADY COMPLETE.** All three gym scenes implement the grow/shrink animation as required. The `PowerUp` lifecycle class provides `currentScale` (0 → 1 → 0) through GROWING/HOLDING/SHRINKING/DESPAWNED states, and all scenes correctly apply it.

The `PowerUp` lifecycle is unit-tested (43/43 tests pass in `PowerUp.test.ts`).

No new implementation work is required.

## Related work (from find_related)

- AH-0MTCO0M3C002Y67S — GymPowerUps scene wiring (ship, spawn, collect, HUD) (completed)
- AH-0MTCNZ1WN007N1FL — Unit tests: HUD model & scene attachability (completed)
- README.md, docs/Game Design Document.md — matched relevant keywords

## Goal
Create the deterministic, pure-logic test suite that locks the explosion VFX contract before the implementation lands. Tests run without rendering and use a seeded RNG + fake timers.

## Context
Parent AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V needs a shared particle helper. This is the test-first feature — no implementation yet, just the spec suite that F2–F6 must satisfy. Keeps colour/pattern/geometry math pure and unit-testable per Constraints (Phaser 4.2.1 + Vitest).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1:** Count scaling is locked: `scaledCount(size)` is linear with `size/referenceSize`, clamped to 8–80, verified at small (e.g. Swarm), standard (Scout/Diver/Tank/Phaser ~20–40) and large (Boss/player ~50–80) sizes.
- [ ] **AC2:** Colour jitter helper stays centred: 100% of emitted colours are within Δ around the base colour (HSL hue ±15–20°, slight sat/light variance); tested against all palette colours (SCOUT 0x00ff00, DIVER 0xffff00, TANK 0xff6600, PHASER 0xff00ff, SWARM 0x0066ff, BOSS 0xff0000, SHIP 0x00ffff).
- [ ] **AC3:** Geometry contracts asserted: radial burst spreads directions uniformly 0–2π with speed spread; ring emits at shared radius/speed forming a circle; implosion-then-burst has a short inward phase (~80–120 ms) then outward burst.
- [ ] **AC4:** Combinator splits verified: single pattern = 1/1, two patterns = 1/2+1/2, three patterns = 1/3+1/3+1/3 (remainder distributed deterministically).
- [ ] **AC5:** Lifecycle/teardown asserted: particles fade alpha 1→0 and shrink to 0 over 300–500 ms then auto-destroy; SHUTDOWN/teardown leaves zero leaked particles (fake timers + destroy spies).

## Key Files
- src/vfx/explosionParticles.test.ts

## Notes
Vertical slice Phase A tracer depends on this. Use seeded RNG so assertions are deterministic. No Phaser rendering in pure helpers.

## Goal
Build the reusable spawnExplosionParticles(scene,x,y,baseColor,size,opts) helper plus tunable constants in one place.

## Context
Parent AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V. Backbone for all VFX. Satisfies the contract locked by sibling AH-0MTVH6DQO0016CGJ test suite. Prefer lightweight Graphics particles (fillCircle 2-3px) animated via scene.tweens for testability; keep pure logic separate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1:** src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts exports spawnExplosionParticles(scene,x,y,baseColor,size,opts).
- [ ] **AC2:** Tunable constants exposed in one place (src/core/constants.ts or src/vfx/constants.ts): EXPLOSION_BASE_COUNT (std ~20-40), EXPLOSION_BOSS_COUNT / EXPLOSION_PLAYER_COUNT (~50-80), EXPLOSION_LIFESPAN_MS 300-500, referenceSize, clamp 8-80, pattern speeds/radii.
- [ ] **AC3:** scaledCount(size) = round(base*size/ref), clamped; larger size yields more particles.
- [ ] **AC4:** Particles fade alpha 1->0 while shrinking to 0 over lifespan then auto-destroy; handles tracked for SHUTDOWN cleanup; no leak across scene restarts.
- [ ] **AC5:** Sibling test suite passes against this implementation.

## Key Files
- src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts
- src/core/constants.ts
- src/vfx/constants.ts

## Goal
Implement the three pattern emitters (radial, ring, implosion-then-burst) plus a combinator that splits the size-scaled count evenly across assigned patterns.

## Context
Parent AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V. Depends on shared module and colour jitter siblings. Assignment is via a per-type config map, not hard-coded inline in every entity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1:** Radial burst: uniformly random directions 0-2pi with speed spread scaling with entity size.
- [ ] **AC2:** Ring/shell: particles emitted on a circle at shared radius/speed forming an expanding ring.
- [ ] **AC3:** Implosion-then-explosion: particles drift inward toward centre for a short phase (~80-120 ms) then burst outward.
- [ ] **AC4:** Combinator splits count correctly: 1 pattern = full count, 2 patterns = half each, 3 patterns = third each (deterministic remainder).
- [ ] **AC5:** resolvePatterns(type) returns the assigned Pattern list from config; pattern speeds/radii are tunable constants.

## Key Files
- src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts
- src/vfx/explosionParticles.test.ts

## Goal
All destruction paths trigger the new particle burst as the primary VFX; old ring tween replaced or augmented with no behaviour change beyond VFX.

## Context
Parent AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V. Depends on module, colour, and pattern siblings. Death paths: Scout/Diver/Tank/Phaser/Swarm/Boss destroySelf()->playExplosion() and GymFormationScene _hitPlayer()->_spawnPlayerExplosion() (or GymPlayer hit path). Audio ownership unchanged (scene-owned playDestructionSound vs entity-owned). Reuse SHUTDOWN teardown pattern from AH-0MTPLHLZ3006MOC4.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1:** Scout/Diver/Tank/Phaser/Swarm/Boss playExplosion (Boss _playExplosion) calls the shared helper with effectiveColor/effectiveSize; particle burst is the primary VFX.
- [ ] **AC2:** Player hit path (_spawnPlayerExplosion / GymPlayer hit handling) calls the helper with SHIP_COLOR / SHIP_SIZE.
- [ ] **AC3:** Behaviour preserved: body hidden immediately, no double audio, hit/invulnerability/respawn logic unchanged.
- [ ] **AC4:** SHUTDOWN teardown destroys particle Graphics (playerExplosions plus entity particles); stop->restart of the same scene instance leaks nothing.
- [ ] **AC5:** Existing lineStyle buffer assertions (Scout.test.ts etc.) updated to cover particle colours/counts; entity and scene suites pass.

## Context
